A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Flow of Reasoning work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v4 reports original experiments across six reasoning benchmarks, together with ablations, OOD evaluations, efficiency measurements, and case studies.

after.justification: v6 retains the original empirical study and reports additional component ablations, model-scaling experiments, sampling analyses, and a process-reward variant.

M1.justification: v6 adds FOR+PRM for GSM8K, augmenting the terminal reward with intermediate scores from Qwen2.5-Math-PRM-7B (Section 4.6). This is a task-specific method extension; the core flow formulation, log-variance objective, replay buffer, exploration procedure, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate BlocksWorld, Game24, Rubik’s Cube, 1D-ARC, GSM8K, and PrOntoQA, including the same OOD scenarios. Additional model configurations and sampling budgets retain this coverage. Newly mentioned structured-data, social, and multimodal tasks are future work.

E2.justification: The comparator methods within the corresponding benchmark experiments are retained. Repeated ToT (DFS) searches and larger CoT backbones change evaluation settings rather than comparator methods. FOR+PRM is an extension of the proposed method; newly cited approaches such as DoT are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Game24 changes its reported backbone from Llama-2-13B to Llama-3-8B and its test selection from indices 910–1010 to 100 randomly selected examples. v6 also introduces GPT-4o diversity evaluation, a matched repeated-search budget for ToT, larger and additional model families, and further training-size and inference-sampling settings. These substantially expand and revise the evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v6 Table 8 removes other components jointly with local search, testing component interactions. It adds repeated-search comparisons, robustness across model families and scales, and a GSM8K sampling-budget analysis. Figure 3 revises reward sensitivity results and expands FOR’s training-size analysis. Earlier OOD tests, diversity-prompt experiments, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the general three-repetition mean/standard-deviation convention and single-repetition creativity reporting. v6 adds explicit repeated-search documentation for ToT (DFS), while Table 1 drops v4’s explicit GPT-4o exception to three-run reporting. These are limited changes in repetition documentation; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces several Game24 results: FOR accuracy/diversity changes from 41.00%/1.52 to 48.00%/1.30 under revised settings, so this is not a same-setting improvement. v6 adds FOR+PRM at 62.62% GSM8K accuracy, automated diversity scores, repeated-ToT results, component-interaction results, and larger-model results. Figure 3 also changes sensitivity values. Most other main benchmark scores are retained.

T1.justification: The DAG assumptions, flow relationships, trajectory-balance and log-variance objectives, local-search acceptance rule, and formal diversity/creativity metrics remain unchanged. Appendix B expands the backward-trajectory and trajectory-balance exposition using mathematics already underlying v4, without adding a substantive theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains step-level, reward-proportional GFlowNet training for accurate and diverse reasoning with minimal examples across six benchmarks. The abstract and introduction retain this scope. Changing the conclusion’s task count from five to six corrects an inconsistency with v4’s already reported coverage.

C2.justification: v6 explains that the replay buffer matters more when local search is absent and interprets the new results as evidence of scalability across model sizes and families. It removes v4’s restriction to experiments with models up to 13B parameters and expands future applications. Computational-cost and long-horizon limitations remain.

D1.justification: v6 identifies the PRM, supplies the GPT-4o diversity-evaluation prompt, and specifies A100 memory as 80GB. It omits v4’s explicit description of Python arithmetic execution during Game24 evaluation; this establishes a documentation removal, not necessarily a procedural removal. Existing task prompts, most hyperparameters, and the code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: v6 updates the positioning against GFlowNet–LLM research, including GDPO, red-teaming work, latent-logic extraction, and concurrent mathematical reasoning by Takase et al. It also adds DoT and sources supporting the new models, evaluator, and future applications. The broader related-work framework and most of Appendix A remain intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative undergoes substantial condensation and rewriting across the introduction, related work, experimental settings, result discussions, and conclusion. v6 changes the title terminology, swaps the GSM8K and PrOntoQA sections, simplifies subsection headings, reorganizes the appendices, and moves the rewritten impact statement into the main text.

P2.justification: v6 replaces the single-column preprint layout with a two-column conference layout and extensively resizes and relocates displays. It redraws Figure 3 with changed axes, legends, and FOR curves; adds the sampling plot and evaluator-prompt figure; introduces new tables; and expands GSM8K’s table. Existing case-study diagrams are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The joint ablations, repeated-search comparison, and larger-model evaluations strengthen evidence about component effects and generalization, addressing v4’s explicit model-size limitation. The benefit is tempered by reporting problems: v6 Table 14 labels Table 1’s one-shot CoT scores as five-shot, and Section 4.2 claims best accuracy despite O1-mini’s higher score. Changed Game24 conditions also prevent interpreting its revised scores as direct progress. Overall, the added checks provide a limited net quality improvement.
